source.description: Project HTTP parser source point where the attacker-controlled request buffer is loaded from helper state.

sink.description: Out-of-bounds 4-byte READ performed by the multichar helper when parsing the final GMT token of a too-short If-Modified-Since value.

root_cause.description: The If-Modified-Since parser only checks that the header value is non-empty before calling lwan_parse_rfc_time, rather than requiring the exact RFC time length.

taint_source.description: Unscored fuzzing boundary; the scored source is parse_http_request loading helper->buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled If-Modified-Since header value and length are stored for later date parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: The HTTP request parser loads the attacker-controlled request buffer and dispatches header parsing.
The If-Modified-Since header value is extracted into helper state.
A non-empty but too-short date header is accepted for RFC time parsing.
The parser advances through fixed-width date fields without receiving a validated-length input.
A fixed-width multichar read crosses the valid header value boundary.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker controls the HTTP If-Modified-Since header value. parse_headers stores the value and length, but parse_if_modified_since only checks that the length is nonzero before calling lwan_parse_rfc_time. That time parser assumes a canonical fixed-width RFC timestamp and advances a cursor through weekday, date, time, and final GMT fields. A non-empty but too-short header value can therefore reach the final fixed-width STRING_SWITCH, where string_as_int32 reads four bytes beyond the valid value buffer.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch introduces the canonical header length `sizeof("Wed, 17 Apr 2019 13:59:27 GMT") - 1` and returns unless helper->if_modified_since.raw.len exactly matches it. This blocks short attacker-controlled values before lwan_parse_rfc_time performs fixed-width multichar reads.
